title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 121 (Report on annual general meeting)

content.overview: Every listed public company must prepare the prescribed report on each annual general meeting and file it with the Registrar within thirty days of the meeting's conclusion. Under subsection (3), failure to file attracts a company penalty of ₹1,00,000 and, for continuing failure, a further ₹500 per day up to ₹5,00,000; every officer in default is liable to a penalty of at least ₹25,000 and, for continuing failure, a further ₹500 per day up to ₹1,00,000.

content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 121 (Report on annual general meeting). Every listed public company must prepare, in the prescribed manner, a report on each AGM confirming that the meeting was convened, held and conducted in accordance with the Act and rules. A copy must be filed with the Registrar within thirty days of the AGM's conclusion. Under subsection (3), failure to file before expiry of the period attracts a penalty of ₹1,00,000 for the company; continuing failure attracts a further ₹500 for each day after the first, subject to a maximum of ₹5,00,000. Every officer in default is liable to a penalty of not less than ₹25,000 and, for continuing failure, a further ₹500 for each day after the first, subject to a maximum of ₹1,00,000. The report is distinct from minutes under section 118. The topic remains under source and current-law review.

sections.heading: Duty and scope
sections.body: Every listed public company must prepare a report on each AGM in the prescribed manner, including confirmation that the meeting was convened, held and conducted in accordance with the Act and rules. This report is distinct from minutes under section 118.

sections.heading: Filing deadline
sections.body: A copy of the report must be filed with the Registrar within thirty days of the conclusion of the AGM.

sections.heading: Penalty for default
sections.body: Under subsection (3), the company is liable to a penalty of ₹1,00,000 and, in case of continuing failure, a further penalty of ₹500 for each day after the first, subject to a maximum of ₹5,00,000. Every officer in default is liable to a penalty of not less than ₹25,000 and, for continuing failure, a further penalty of ₹500 for each day after the first, subject to a maximum of ₹1,00,000.

examples.title: Timely AGM report
examples.body: A listed public company records the AGM conclusion date, prepares the prescribed report and files it with the Registrar within thirty days.

examples.title: Continuing filing default
examples.body: When assessing a missed filing, identify the company penalty and the separate penalty applicable to every officer in default, including the continuing-default daily amount and cap.

hypotheticals.question: Does keeping minutes under section 118 replace the section 121 report?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Minutes and the AGM report are distinct statutory obligations. A listed public company must meet the section 121 report and filing requirements where they apply.

hypotheticals.question: A listed public company fails to file its section 121 report and the failure continues. What penalty structure does subsection (3) state?
hypotheticals.analysis: The company is liable to a penalty of ₹1,00,000 and a further ₹500 per day after the first for continuing failure, capped at ₹5,00,000. Every officer in default is liable to at least ₹25,000 and a further ₹500 per day after the first for continuing failure, capped at ₹1,00,000. Verify the current text before applying the penalty in a real matter.

misconceptions.trap: Assuming minutes under section 118 replace the AGM report.
misconceptions.correction: Section 121 is a separate filing duty for listed public companies.

misconceptions.trap: Stating only a company penalty and omitting the separate officer-in-default penalty.
misconceptions.correction: Subsection (3) specifies a penalty for the company and a separate penalty for every officer in default.

misconceptions.trap: Ignoring the daily amount and cap for continuing failure.
misconceptions.correction: State the ₹500-per-day component and the separate maximum for the company and officer in default.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Who must file an AGM report under section 121 and when?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Every listed public company must prepare a report on each AGM in the prescribed manner and file it with the Registrar within thirty days of conclusion of the meeting.
